newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Gist-Brocades 1996 net seen 10 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Gist-Brocades 1996 net seen 10 pct higher.

text.p: Dutch biochemicals and food group Gist-Brocades NV is seen posting solid 10 percent earnings growth in 1996, mainly buoyed by a strong dollar.
Analysts expect full-year net profits of around 158 million guilders to be published Wednesday. Forecasts range from 154 to 160 million guilders, with most clustered around the consensus.
"Gist has given a relatively clear indication on how business fares, which explains the tight range," said Peter Wortel, analyst at Delta Lloyd Bank.
Profit growth is seen braked by pressured penicillin prices, despite Gist being one of the world's lowest cost producers.
Overcapacity on the yeast market will also impact adversely on results, said Patrick Rutten, analyst with Van Lanschot.
On another hand, the company will have benefited from the higher dollar in 1996.
"Gist is a highly dollar-sensitive stock," said Rutten.
Last year, exchange rate fluctuations reduced full-year profits by some 40 million guilders.
Wortel said Gist had a good position in patents, which added to the company's financial strength.
"They have expansion possibilities abroad," said Wortel, adding Gist had was one of the leading researchers in its field.
Warnings from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Gist's penicillin production methods were not seen having a measurable impact on 1996 results.
"I think the case has been blown up a little," said Wortel, adding he expected a solution to be found fairly soon.
He said the FDA's warning might have a slightly negative effect on Gist's position on the short term.
"I am very curious to hear what the company will say about it," said Rutten.
Analysts said partnerships like the one with SmithKline Beecham enhanced Gist's longer-term prospects.
"Partnerships are essential in order to survive, because R&D costs in the sector are very high for a small company like Gist-Brocades," said Wortel.
Long-term profit growth prospects for the firm were seen as moderately positive.
"I don't expect the company to outperform its market," said Wortel, adding he foresaw an annual 10 to 11 percent profit growth for the next couple of years.
Gist-Brocades is active in various segments of the biotechnology sector.

In 1995, the firm's Industrial Pharmaceutical Products Division turned over 666 million guilders, the Bakery Ingredients Division 735 million guilders and the Food Specialties Division booked sales of 298 million guilders.
